sections.h2: Which Suwannee County offices touch a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Value, billing and recording each sit with a different elected office in Live Oak. The appraiser sets what a parcel is worth, the collector sends and takes in payment, and the clerk keeps the deed records. Millage rates come from the local governments that levy tax, and they multiply against the appraiser's figure.

Suwannee became Florida's thirty-seventh county on December 21, 1858, carved out of western Columbia County. It borrows its name from the river that begins in Georgia's Okefenokee Swamp and travels some 240 miles to the Gulf; more than 70 springs along the way pull in divers. Many Suwannee parcels are river frontage, spring-country lots and rural acreage, so legal descriptions deserve a careful look.

  • Property appraiser: 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite B, Live Oak. Phone 386-362-1385. Weekday hours 8:30 to 5:00, closed on county holidays.
  • Tax collector: 215 Pine Ave SW, Suite A, Live Oak. Phone 386-362-2816. The collector serves county residents, with exceptions for property owners.
  • Clerk of the circuit court: records deeds and mortgages and conducts tax deed sales.

The appraiser's calendar shows the offices closed for Good Friday, Veterans Day (observed) and the Thursday and Friday of Thanksgiving, among other holidays, so plan filings around those days.

sections.h2: Which dates control a Suwannee County tax year?
sections.html:
Four dates do most of the work: January 1, March 1, November and March 31. Value and residency are fixed on January 1. Exemption forms go to the appraiser by March 1, and that deadline also covers agricultural classification (DR-482), conservation classification (DR-482C) and the conservation exemption (DR-418C). Business owners file tangible personal property returns (DR-405) by April 1.

Bills then cover one calendar year and carry early-pay savings, listed below as the collector prints them.

Savings for early payment printed by the Suwannee collector
Month paidSavings
November4%
December3%
January2%
February1%

The collector says the postmark controls for mail sent before April 1, and the gross amount is due March 31. Payments after April 30 must be in certified funds, and personal checks mailed or left in the drop box are sent back. The same page says the March 31 date is also the deadline to apply for indigent relief or adjust non-ad valorem assessments.

sections.h2: What if a Suwannee County tax bill is left unpaid?
sections.html:
Taxes turn delinquent April 1, and the collector says real estate picks up a 3% penalty that day. Tax sale certificates are then sold on unpaid accounts on or before June 1, which brings extra charges. Anyone holding a certificate waits two years from the April 1 after issuance before asking for a tax deed, and cannot demand payment from the owner during that stretch.

A sale never wipes out the debt. Ask the Suwannee County Tax Collector for a written payoff covering every open year before you sign a contract, and give a copy to the title company.

  • A buyer under a recorded contract for deed is on the list of people notified before a tax deed sale.
  • On homestead land, the opening bid at a tax deed sale includes half of the latest assessed value.
  • Land that draws no bidder goes on a county list, and the county can buy it for the opening bid.

sections.h2: Does Suwannee County offer installments or deferral?
sections.html:
Both exist. The installment plan requires an estimated bill above $100 and an application on file before May 1. Quarter payments land June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, discounted 6%, 4.5% and 3% on the first three and not discounted on the last. A missed first payment drops the parcel from the plan, and owners who stay in are enrolled again every year without reapplying.

Deferral is for homesteads with a low income against the tax. The collector says an owner can postpone the portion above 5% of household income, or above 3% from age 65, and can postpone all of it under $10,000 of income ($12,000 from age 70). The mortgage cannot exceed 70% of assessed value, liens and deferred tax together are capped at 85%, and insurance must name the collector as payee. Applications are due January 31 after bills are mailed. Deferred tax earns interest and sits as a lien on the house.

sections.h2: How do homestead and Save Our Homes change a Suwannee County sale?
sections.html:
Homestead trims taxable value only while you live in the house, and the benefit does not travel with the title. The appraiser's list shows a $25,000 homestead exemption, $5,000 for disabled veterans, and $5,000 each for widows and widowers. Title must be in your name with the house as your permanent home on January 1. Ask the appraiser about the second homestead layer that applies to value above $50,000 for non-school taxes.

Under Save Our Homes, assessed value on a homestead can rise each year by no more than the lower of 3% or inflation. Selling resets the parcel to full just value the next January 1, which means a buyer can face a larger bill than you paid. If you move to another Florida homestead, portability can carry part of the saved value to it, provided the move happens inside three years counted from January 1 of the year you gave up the old home. File DR-501T alongside the new application by March 1.

  • Renting the house out can end the homestead.
  • Forms DR-501DV, DR-501M and DR-501SC cover veterans, deployed service members and low-income seniors.
  • Seniors send income information by June 1.

sections.h2: What should a Suwannee County seller expect at closing?
sections.html:
Your closing agent divides this year's tax with the buyer, which makes the closing date set your share. Older unpaid years are cleared from the proceeds. The collector also asks sellers to send the tax notice on to the new owner or bring it back to the office.

Recording of the deed falls to the clerk, who also collects the state deed tax at the time of filing.

  • Ask for a payoff before listing when a year was skipped.
  • Have the appraiser update ownership and remove your exemption after the sale.
  • Keep the signed closing statement.

sections.h2: When does a direct cash sale make sense in Suwannee County?
sections.html:
A direct purchase suits an inherited house, a vacant one or a parcel that has fallen behind on tax. The buyer takes it as is, so you skip repairs and showings, and the tax balance comes out of the price at the closing table.

Weigh any offer against what listing would leave after commission, repairs and the carrying months. Verify that the legal description and parcel number on the deed match the appraiser's file before you sign.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay Suwannee County property tax?
faqs.a: March 31 is the last day for the gross amount. The collector reports 4% off for November payments, 3% for December, 2% for January and 1% for February, judged by postmark before April 1.

faqs.q: When must I apply for homestead in Suwannee County?
faqs.a: March 1 is the cutoff at the property appraiser's office on Pine Avenue in Live Oak, 386-362-1385. The home must be titled to you and be your permanent residence on January 1.

faqs.q: Can I spread Suwannee County property tax over the year?
faqs.a: Yes, when the estimated bill tops $100 and your signed form reaches the collector before May 1. Four payments fall on June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31.

faqs.q: What happens on April 1 to an unpaid Suwannee County bill?
faqs.a: It turns delinquent and a 3% penalty applies to real estate, according to the collector. Certificates on unpaid accounts are sold on or before June 1. Call 386-362-2816 for a payoff.

faqs.q: Who covers the deed stamp tax on a Suwannee County sale?
faqs.a: Florida holds every signer of the deed answerable, whichever side the contract assigns it to. The charge is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, collected by the clerk when the deed is recorded.
